question: Which Swiss authorizations share recorded ATC classifications or ancestors with a selected medicine, and which connections require package-derived classifications?
status: Exploratory within-domain transfer; design fixed before outcome extraction and native timings. Source schemas and the anchor-selection result were inspected during design.
selection: D0 authorizations with dictionary-listed seven-character direct and package codes; group by first direct-code letter, hash-order classes using transfer-20261025:<letter>, retain first three; select minimum SHA256 transfer-20261025:<authorization> within each class.
hierarchy: ATC dictionary entries linked only to their immediately preceding standard prefix (lengths 1,3,4,5,7), if present; absent parent is not skipped.
scope: Source-record classifications and common ATC ancestors; no equivalence, indication, substitution or reimbursement conclusion.
ablation: Disable package-derived classifications on both sides; retain all product identities and the hierarchy.
reference: Independent Python source grouping and prefix enumeration; no database outputs used to build expected answers. Full witness IDs, source-record lists, common ancestors, codes and depths retained.

timing.transport: identical local HTTP JSON endpoint contract; backend execution, full response transfer and decoding timed; driver-specific serialization documented

scaling: Disconnected copies of the same source-derived graph, including hierarchy; every copy is queried. Controls storage and answer-volume growth, not new medical diversity or denser topology.
updates: D0-to-D1 answer changes reconstructed offline; additional native timings measure D1 retrieval and model loading, not the original build-refresh-retrieval scenario.
reporting: All selected tasks, raw repetitions, plans, answer hashes, environment, construction time and rule ablation. No winner-dependent task selection or post-timing tuning. Any implementation repairs logged separately.
